events.title: Pocahontas Marries John Rolfe
events.description: In Virginia, Pocahontas, the daughter of a powerful Powhatan leader, married English colonist John Rolfe. The wedding took place in the young Jamestown colony.
events.significance: The marriage helped bring a period of relative peace between the Powhatan and the English settlers, often called the Peace of Pocahontas. It remains one of the best-known and most debated episodes of early colonial America.

events.title: Europeans Reach Easter Island
events.description: Dutch explorer Jacob Roggeveen sighted and landed on a remote Pacific island on Easter Sunday. He named it Easter Island for the day.
events.significance: This was the first recorded European contact with Rapa Nui, home to the famous moai statues. It opened a new chapter in the island's history and in the world's fascination with it.

events.title: Booker T. Washington Is Born
events.description: Booker Taliaferro Washington was born into slavery in Hale's Ford, Virginia. After emancipation he pursued an education against great odds.
events.significance: Washington became one of the most influential Black educators and leaders of his era. He led the Tuskegee Institute and shaped national debate on education and progress after Reconstruction.

events.title: The War of the Pacific Begins
events.description: Chile declared war on Bolivia and Peru after Bolivia had declared war on Chile. The conflict was fought over valuable nitrate and mineral resources in the Atacama region.
events.significance: Chile's victory reshaped South American borders. Bolivia lost its coastline, a loss that still shapes its politics and diplomacy today.

events.title: Rosenbergs Sentenced to Death
events.description: A federal judge sentenced Julius and Ethel Rosenberg to death after they were convicted of conspiracy to commit espionage for the Soviet Union. It was a tense moment in the early Cold War.
events.significance: The case became one of the most controversial trials in American history. The couple were executed in 1953, and debate over the fairness of the case has continued ever since.
